html:
The first commercial bank chartered in the United States, approved by the Congress of the Confederation on 26 May 1781 and opened in Philadelphia in January 1782. It also acted as the country's first central bank in all but name.

It was the plan of Robert Morris, the Superintendent of Finance, during the Revolutionary War. Congress was nearly broke and its paper money had collapsed. The bank lent money to the government, issued its own notes, which people trusted more, and helped pay for the final campaigns of the war. Its start-up capital was backed by silver lent by France.

After the war it faced attacks from those who feared a rich man's monopoly, and Pennsylvania took away its charter for a time. It continued as an ordinary state bank. The idea of a national bank passed to Alexander Hamilton's First Bank of the United States in 1791. The Bank of North America lasted, through mergers, into the 20th century.
sum: The first commercial bank chartered in the United States, approved by the Congress of the Confederation on 26 May 1781 and opened in Philadelphia in January 1782. It also acted as the country's first central bank in all but name.
